abstract.t: This document defines a cross-protocol orchestration framework for post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) key rotation across heterogeneous networked environments. It specifies the sequencing, signaling, and rollback mechanisms required to coordinate ML-DSA and SLH-DSA key epoch transitions across TLS, PKIX, OAuth, ACME, BRSKI, WIMSE, RATS, and SCITT protocol stacks without service interruption.
This revision (-03) expands the orchestration state machine, adds conformance criteria for tenant-isolated PKI environments, and aligns epoch signaling with draft-vicente-lamps-rotation-envelope.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: PQC migration requires coordinated key rotation across multiple protocol layers simultaneously. Ad-hoc per-protocol rotation creates epoch skew: a TLS endpoint may accept connections under epoch N+1 while a dependent OCSP responder still operates under epoch N, causing verification failures. This document defines a cross-protocol orchestration framework that eliminates epoch skew by providing a unified rotation state machine, inter-protocol signaling, and tenant-aware rollback.

This revision (-03) aligns the epoch signal format with draft-vicente-lamps-rotation-envelope and adds conformance criteria for multi-tenant PKI deployments (draft-vicente-pquip-multitenant-pki-requirements).

dl.dd: A discrete interval of PQC signing-key validity, identified by a monotonically increasing integer (epoch_id).
The system component responsible for sequencing epoch transitions across protocol stacks.
The condition in which different protocol endpoints operate under different epoch_id values simultaneously, causing verification failures.
The artifact defined in draft-vicente-lamps-rotation-envelope conveying prior and new epoch certificate bindings.

section.name: Orchestration State Machine
section.t: The rotation orchestrator MUST implement the following states:

ol.li: IDLE: No rotation in progress. Current epoch_id is authoritative.
PREPARE: New ML-DSA key pair generated. Rotation Envelope constructed. Pre-position signals sent to dependent protocol stacks.
COMMIT: All dependent stacks have acknowledged readiness. New epoch_id becomes authoritative. Old epoch remains valid for a configurable grace period.
DRAIN: Grace period active. Both epoch_id N and N+1 accepted. Connections using epoch N are drained.
COMPLETE: Grace period expired. Epoch N revoked. Rotation Envelope published to SCITT transparency log.
ROLLBACK: Entered from PREPARE or COMMIT on error. Epoch N+1 abandoned. Epoch N remains authoritative.

section.t: The orchestrator MUST NOT transition from PREPARE to COMMIT until all registered protocol stacks have acknowledged epoch readiness. Unacknowledged stacks MUST trigger ROLLBACK after a configurable timeout (default: 300 seconds).

section.name: Inter-Protocol Epoch Signaling
section.t: Protocol stacks participating in orchestrated rotation MUST implement an epoch readiness signal. The signal MUST convey:

ul.li: A readiness status: READY, NOT_READY, or ERROR.

section.t: Signals MUST be integrity-protected using the current epoch's ML-DSA signing key. Signal transport is stack-specific and out of scope; recommended transports include HTTPS with mutual ML-DSA authentication and MQTT with ML-DSA-signed payloads.

section.name: Tenant-Isolated Rotation
section.t: In multi-tenant PKI deployments (draft-vicente-pquip-multitenant-pki-requirements), rotation orchestration MUST be scoped per tenant. Tenant A's epoch transition MUST NOT affect Tenant B's epoch state. The orchestrator MUST maintain separate state machine instances per tenant identifier. Cross-tenant epoch correlation signals MUST NOT be emitted.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The orchestration framework eliminates epoch skew, the primary cause of PQC migration-induced verification failures. The ROLLBACK state ensures that a failed rotation does not leave any protocol stack in an inconsistent epoch state. Rotation Envelopes published to SCITT provide an auditable record of all epoch transitions. Operators MUST monitor epoch_id consistency across all registered protocol stacks using the observability mechanisms defined in draft-vicente-pquip-pqc-readiness-gaps.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA is requested to register a media type for the inter-protocol epoch readiness signal format defined in this document.
